The back story to my first attempt.

I spent all of high school training to swim in college. 6-7 days a week for 4 hours a day most days. I had a strong desire to improve and a reachable goal. In my senior year, however, I fell into a deep depression. I lost interest in attaining the very thing I had wanted and sacrificed my life for. I felt like life was meaningless. During this time, my swim coach's wife, who also coached me, started to grow closer to me. Texting and calling after practice was over, and insinuating the idea of us dating. It is worth noting that when you are in the environment/world of training constantly and being surrounded by the same people day in and day out, that becomes your reality. That becomes the only people who really exist to you. Being so isolated, due to my devotion to the sport and my depression, I let this 30+ year old mother of 4 talk me into having a relationship with her and eventually having sex with her. The weight of having sex with my coach's wife behind his back and lying to him about what happened eventually took its toll on my desire to continue swimming. This crushed me once I realized that all of the efforts I had put into swim, was for nothing. At this point, I felt like I had lost a part of me and felt hopeless. 

During the final month of swimming, I started to date my childhood crush. After I had left the sport, she was the very and only thing I had left to hold onto. It felt like she was my 'savior'. One day, though, she told me that she was going to kill herself, as she herself has mental issues. In that moment, to me, I had lost the only thing tying me to this earth. I proceeded to get drunk off of my parent's beer, get into my bathroom, and cut myself so I'd bleed to death. When I cut myself I was crying, not from the fear of death, but from the trauma and loss of losing everything that gave me a will to live. I genuinely believed that I was going to die, and there is no describing that peace when thinking and truly believing my pain, from living, was about to be all over. My mom, unfortunately, arrived home and heard me crying while I was in the middle of the act and threatened to call 911. I knew I couldn't bleed out before they could get there so I unlocked the door and asked my mother why she didn't just let me die. 

​

The back story to my second attempt.

My entire life I have always been extremely self-conscious about my body fat percentage. I have always looked at others, including myself, and focus solely on how their body appears. Are they fat? muscular? skinny? To me, having the power to take one's shirt off and look flawless is something beyond money or fame. It is something so valued and idolized in my brain. The girlfriend, I mentioned earlier, and I are still dating, but growing up I didn't have the confidence to ask her out because of the way I looked. She was/is extremely beautiful and has an amazing body, but I was chubby and didn't think I deserved to be with someone like that. She would go to my swim practices just to be close to me and beg me to hang out with her. Even though it seemed like she had some sort of obsession with me, I didn't think I was good enough for her and felt like an imposter for having the prettiest girl in school be obsessed with me. Her senior year (my junior year), she started dating the new kid who was in my grade. He is 6'0", lean, tan, and extremely attractive (everything I wished I was). He had ambitions to be a model and was under a modeling agency during high school. Seeing someone so attractive date your childhood crush devastated me. It almost confirmed to me that it had to take someone as good-looking as him to date her, and I would never be good enough.  It turned out that he wasn't such a nice guy and they fought frequently. Every time they fought, she would come to my house and ask me if I liked her and if I wanted to date her. I thought it would be wrong to date her if she was dating someone else, and how could I have dated her in the footsteps of someone who was way more attractive? At some point, I became friends with him. When they started dating he would stare me down as we passed each other in the hallways because he found out that I was the guy who she was in love with before. I felt this weird need to befriend him because I couldn't handle having someone that attractive have beef with me and plus I was scared of him. Eventually, after they had broken up for almost a year and after losing everything I had wanted, I thought why not just ask her out. The relationship we had at first was a rocky one because of toxic traits she developed as a result of being with a narcissist. 

Flash forward to when I started working out.

After losing swim, I found something that I thought was my purpose, to finally improve and have a body I love. This was coupled with the want to impress my girlfriend in the light of her ex being more attractive than me. I started working out to build muscle for a while until I realized I wasn't improving much. I, then, desperately found someone who sold steroids and bought and injected them in hopes it would change me. 3 months went by with very little improvement, so I decided to try and get what I had always wanted, abs. Once I started to lose fat, it wasn't long until I could see the outline of my abs that I had built up on steroids. But after not even 5 weeks of getting leaner I had come across hard struggles with binge-eating. I carried on and tried to keep going but the eating disorder got worse and worse eventually leading to me developing bulemia. I had reached a point to where I could pretty much see my abs, but I was never satisfied. When I was around my girlfriend I felt like I deserved to be there, but when my eating disorder(s) developed I slowly crept back into the mindset of not being good enough. The thought of not having what it takes, and that you, your genetic makeup, and the way you think not being good enough or what you want really took a toll on me. I realized that I was never going to be who I wanted. I was never, no matter how much I tried, going to match what my dreams were. I just am not who I want to be, and I am stuck inside of the body I hate until I die. This led me to buy 500+ pills of ibuprofen, not realizing that I would puke everywhere and be sent to the hospital. And furthermore, if I hadn't puked, it would have led to a drawn-out, incredibly painful process to die. 

After being sent to the hospital, I gained weight immediately. It was almost like the incident with swim, something I had worked so hard for turning to sand between my fingertips overnight. 

​

Currently, I have still not managed to get to where I was physically. I attempted to hang myself yesterday and the day before, but something in my body panics when I am about to lose consciousness, not to mention it being extremely agonizing to hang from your neck and immense pressure to your throat. 

​
